description: Delay and resonator in one: a mode switch turns the delay line into a tuned resonator that a trigger plucks, and the delay side can take its time from a clock

params.text: In delay mode it sets the delay time, or the division of the clock when one is patched; in resonator mode it sets the pitch, two octaves per turn
Sets how much of the output is fed back, so how many repeats there are, or in resonator mode how long the resonance rings
Sets the level of the signal going into the delay line, reading out in dB
In delay mode it crossfades the MIX output between dry and delayed; in resonator mode it is a fine adjustment on the pitch, an octave per turn
Divides the delay time by one, two or three, and in resonator mode raises the pitch by nought, one or two octaves instead
Switches the module between the delay and the resonator, which changes how the TIME, REPEAT, MIX and 1V/OCT controls are read
Chooses which way the delay line is read, out of REV, H-REV and NORM

inputs.text: In resonator mode a pitch input tracking one volt per octave; in delay mode it picks the clock division, ten divisions per volt
Raises the feedback, 10V covering the whole of the repeat knob's travel
The audio fed into the delay line, ±10V taken as full scale
In resonator mode a rising edge past 1V plucks the resonator; in delay mode the same jack shifts the dry and delayed balance, 10V covering the whole of the mix knob's travel
In delay mode a rising edge past 1V sets the delay time from the gap between edges; in resonator mode the jack modulates the pitch, a fifth of a volt to the octave

outputs.text: The dry and delayed signals mixed according to the mix knob

notes: with a cable in the trigger jack the module behaves as a resonator that only sounds when a trigger arrives; with that jack empty it is an ordinary delay.
menu: LP filter :  — switches a lowpass filter into the wet signal before it is mixed into the MIX output, and prints its own state after the colon
